prize_parts.citation: For discoveries of the incretin physiology of glucagon-like peptide-1 and the identification of its active form, which enabled GLP-1-based therapies for type 2 diabetes and obesity

statement.case_for: My preferred configuration is unchanged: a single-part prize on B033 for Drucker, Holst and Mojsov. The six round-1 files converge on it, but I treat that as a reason to test the names, not as evidence. The scientific chain is complete and independently confirmed: gut-derived GLP-1 potentiates glucose-dependent insulin secretion, the active truncated peptide was identified and made available, receptor signalling and degradation explain why long-acting agonists work, and large randomized trials show glycaemic, weight, cardiovascular and renal benefit. The discovery is mature and its effect on patients is large. Having reread the exchange, I would write the citation so that it claims the physiology and the identification of the active form, and does not claim a first discovery of the incretin concept or of GLP-1 itself. That wording answers the chair's question about priority without pretending the Mojsov-Habener record has been adjudicated.
statement.case_against: The reservation I weigh most is still attribution, and round 1 did not remove it: nobody has produced evidence that settles Mojsov versus Habener and colleagues, and three slots cannot honour Holst, Drucker, Mojsov, Knudsen and the early contributors outside the list. A physiology-only trio can be read as a judgement against translation, since patients receive liraglutide and semaglutide. I also accept that tidy credit is a real virtue of B036, and that if the committee finds the priority record against Mojsov, the fallback should be decided on documented evidence, not by default. If that happens I would weigh Drucker and Holst with a different third name or a switch to B036, rather than put Knudsen in by reflex.

responses.point: Marie Wahren-Herlenius opened with Knudsen in place of Mojsov and in round 1 described that as the weaker choice, while saying her confidence in the exact trio is lower than in the achievement.
responses.response: I note that you withdrew the Knudsen substitution, and I think you are right that the unsettled Mojsov question is better handled by wording than by changing who is named. I would make that concrete: the citation should say identification of the active peptide, and the committee should read the priority evidence before the final vote, not assume it. Where I still differ from your hesitation is that lower confidence in one name should not move the whole configuration. If the evidence goes against Mojsov, the fallback should keep the discovery logic, so Drucker and Holst plus a differently justified third name or a smaller group, not an industrial name added to preserve a count of three. I do not see Knudsen's contribution as minor; it belongs to a different kind of achievement than the one this prize would define.

responses.point: Thomas Perlmann argues that B036 (Mori and Walter) has a coherent discovery story through IRE1, HAC1 splicing and the transcriptional response, but that its medical consequences are mostly indirect and PERK and ATF6 contributors are uncredited. He asked that the committee state the attribution uncertainty openly and focus the final discussion on allocation.
responses.response: I agree with the request to separate agreement on the topic from agreement on the names, and I have tried to do that above. On B036 I have moved slightly: in round 1 I ranked it sixth in the opening and treated it as a basic-science option, but your point about the IRE1 to HAC1 route makes the two-name credit more convincing than I gave it credit for, and the PERK and ATF6 omission is a smaller problem than the three-way split in B033. I still place it second this year because the clinical consequences are indirect, whereas B033 has a demonstrated patient effect. I now list B036 as my first alternative, ahead of the B011 I named in round 1.

responses.point: Per Svenningsson, as chair, regards B047 as narrower, since it concerns one mechanism for one disease in a younger field and leaves out SMN1 and SMN2 genetics, and so better suited to a later year; he also holds that the evidence does not support waiting on B033.
responses.response: I agree on timing for B033 and nothing in the safety discussion makes me want to defer it. On B047 your objection is fair about breadth and about the genetic groundwork, and I concede that the experimental contributors beyond Krainer and Bennett are a real gap in the credited names. I still keep it as a second alternative because its chain from splicing mechanism to approved therapy is direct and its two-name credit is unusually clean for a translational achievement. I would not rank it above B036 and I accept that a later year may serve it better.

responses.point: Rickard Sandberg argues that attribution cost outweighs method impact for B011, since any three-name optogenetics trio omits a strong claimant (Bamberg, Boyden or Miesenboeck), and that tidy credit on a mostly indirect discovery should not outrank a harder but workable B033.
responses.response: On B011 you persuaded me. In round 1 I kept it as my first alternative on the strength of method impact, but I have no principled line for a three-name cut, and a prize seen as unfair to a leading contributor carries a lasting cost, so I have dropped it from my alternatives. On your second point I agree: attribution cleanliness is a virtue but does not by itself outweigh a larger demonstrated effect, which is why B036 is an alternative here and not my choice. I would add that I do not accept that your caution about the Mojsov question should be read as conceding her claim; we are saying we need the evidence.

uncertainties: Whether Mojsov's claim to identifying active GLP-1(7-36) can be separated from the work of Habener and colleagues, who are not on the credited list; this cannot be resolved from the supplied material and remains the main risk to my configuration.

Whether the prize is defined as physiology and identification only, or whether Knudsen should accompany a basic scientist under some other citation; I judge the first the more defensible, but it has a cost.
How much weight the still-accumulating long-term safety and durability data in obesity should carry; I do not think it justifies waiting.
statement.conflict_note: No change. My documented co-authors (Betsholtz, Ernfors, Frisen, Castelo-Branco, Lundeberg, Kharchenko) and my co-authorship of the 2016 spatial-transcriptomics paper involve no credited name on any shortlisted ballot. I note that Rickard Sandberg is a co-author of mine, as he disclosed, on work unrelated to any shortlisted candidate, and I do not regard it as grounds for recusal.
